title: XPRIZE Wildfire winners spotted fires within 10 min—but couldn’t stop them
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: Wildfire detection from space and firefighting drones featured among the finalists honored in the $11 million XPRIZE Wildfire competition. Although no team walked away with either of the two grand prizes, such technologies could prove helpful as the world grapples with the growing costs of worsening wildfire disasters. The competition’s First Prize track for space-based wildfire detection challenged teams to accurately detect all fires across a large swath of Australia within 10 minutes. A second Autonomous Response Prize track challenged teams to autonomously detect and put out a high-risk fire located somewhere within rural Alaska while ignoring decoy fires—all within 10 minutes of the fire igniting. “We want to be able to prepare and provide tools for firefighters to really allow them to do the best job,” said Andrea Santy , program director of XPRIZE Wildfire , in an interview with Ars. “They're great at what they do, but it's unfair to continue to put them in harm's way when there's technology coming online that can help keep them safe, keep communities safe, and protect ecosystems.” Read full article Comments

Discord had announced a somewhat different plan for age checks in February, but scrapped it amid backlash from users concerned about privacy. title: How this lesbian watering hole became the most (in)famous bar in the world
body: The nightlife minutiae of a small town in Massachusetts may not seem like traditional fodder for a 24-hour news cycle. But turn that drama into a more-than-1,500-word Boston Globe article, sprinkled with ap ritifs for online discourse? Well, that's a recipe for virality. That's what happened when the Globe reported on a recent public skirmish between community members and the owners of Last Ditch Bar and Arts Venue, a lesbian bar and event space in Greenfield, a town of just 17,000 people. SEE ALSO: YouTube's microdrama boom is getting bigger The Last Ditch is one of just 36 lesbian bars in the U.S. , as chronicled by the Lesbian Bar Project. It's a nightlife outlier amid a post-COVID bar and club scene that has had to reckon with a decline in public socialization let alone one that has addressed the alarming decline of number of lesbian bars across the country long before the global pandemic. But the bar's reputation as a gathering place for Greenfield's sapphic community is now marred by a dramatic series of events that started with a single Instagram post . The Aug. 31 alert to customers began as an explanation of the venue's updated mask policy. Where the space used to require KN-95 masks at all times, Last Ditch was moving towards more mask-less events specifically opening up Saturday nights to maskless customers. The response from commenters online was a no-holds-barred flurry of irate messages, accusations of ableism and racism, and even calls for violence from former customers who said their previously safe space had been compromised. title: YouTube promises custom feeds and a lot more AI later this year
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: The annual Made on YouTube event has just wrapped up, offering an early look at the features you can expect to come to Google's dominant online streaming platform in the coming months. Yes, there's plenty of AI for both viewers and creators, but there's also a handful of non-AI updates mixed in there, too. The design of YouTube's homepage feed comes under fire often, but the platform is preparing to give you more options. With Custom Feeds, you'll be able to add new tabs to the YouTube interface with content of your choice. To create a feed, just type a description and let YouTube populate the page. You can refine your description and rate video suggestions to tune the Custom Feed. Google says you'll be able to save "multiple" feeds without specifying the exact number. This feature will roll out soon in the US for web, mobile, and TV users. Interacting on YouTube will also change later this year. The platform will finally add the option to post GIFs in comments, which has apparently been a common request for some time. The comment box will let you search for popular animated thumbnails and post them on both regular videos and YouTube Shorts. The YouTube direct messaging feature is also adding support for group chat, but it's only going to be available in the US, UK, Singapore, Brazil, and some European countries to start. title: Netflix releases trailer for Brad Bird's Ray Gunn
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Brad Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He's back with a new animated feature, Ray Gunn , coming to Netflix in December, described as a neo-noir science-fiction mystery. Netflix recently released the official trailer, chock-full of retro-futuristic elements, like flying cars, jet packs, laser guns, aliens, and yes, a sultry femme fatale. Color us among those now eagerly awaiting the film's release. Bird has been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987's Batteries Not Included with Bird—"stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers," the director said earlier this year. The film's inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s' " Planet Claire " (a personal favorite) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini's theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn . Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a pun on raygun , of course). "It’s film noir and a hard-boiled detective story, but it’s got a lot more comedy and a lot more action than the average film noir,” said Bird . Read full article Comments

title: Gallup poll reveals widespread global AI optimism, not doom and gloom
body: People around the world are largely optimistic about artificial intelligence , according to a new Gallup poll. At the same time, a majority of respondents reported they've never actually used the new technology. The Gallup-Microsoft AI survey , published Sept. 23 as part of the polling company's ongoing research with Microsoft, found that positive feelings about AI outweigh negative ones in 34 of the first 37 countries to complete fieldwork this year. The United States, Egypt, and Palestine were the only exceptions. Gallup says the study will eventually cover 140 countries. SEE ALSO: Grieving people prefer AI bots that speak as dead loved ones, study suggests Across the 37 countries, 72 percent of AI-aware adults reported at least one positive emotion toward the technology, compared with 41 percent who reported at least one negative emotion. Curiosity was the most common response, with a median of 64 percent saying AI makes them feel curious. Worry was the most common negative emotion, at a median of 32 percent. Views on AI's broader impact were also mostly positive. In 29 countries, more people said AI would mostly help their country than harm it. The contrast between the United States and China was particularly revealing: 93 percent of Chinese respondents said AI will help their country. The United States ranked near the bottom, at 36 percent, just above Egypt and Bangladesh. Gallup noted that optimism doesn't always track with usage. title: New YouTube Music features will answer all your questions about a song or artist

On Wednesday, YouTube announced new features for Ask Music in the YouTube Music app. The feature is currently mainly used to create personalized stations and find music based on your mood. Now, however, YouTube Music users will be able to discover new music based on the songs they're listening to. Users can ask Ask Music for information about songs and albums that inspired a particular track. If they really like a song, they can even use Ask Music to find podcasts and podcast episodes featuring the artist behind it or get more details about the track. During a demo at the Made on YouTube event, YouTuber Derrick Gee showcased how users could ask Ask Music who played bass on a track and then find other songs featuring that musician. Ask Music can also help listeners find songs that sampled a particular track. Podcasts are also a big part of YouTube Music and that's where the new Your Podcast Lineup feature comes in. With Your Podcast Lineup, users can create an AI-generated podcast about other podcasts recommended by YouTube Music based on their interests. title: Kids arent learning to type anymore
body: Long live Mavis Beacon. If you're unfamiliar with the name, she was the not-entirely-real icon behind classroom software that taught generations of students touch typing. Beacon was a celebrity of early digital literacy, with generations of learners collectively misremembering her as a real-life elite typer not just a made-up name attached to the likeness of model Ren e L'Esperance. Still, Beacon became an avatar for the digital dreams of the pre-Y2K generation. The software, full name "Mavis Beacon Teaches Typing," was an entry point to the world of technology for thousands of children who would later grow into a computer-skilled workforce. Before entering the rat race, though, these students would be required to attend "Computer Lab," where they would visit typing.com to compete for the highest WPM ("words per minute"). Now, most kids don't go to a computer lab. They boot up their personal Chromebooks at their desks, log onto their school's assignment portal, complete their tasks with help from AI, and go back to their phones or iPads. Concern about technology's impact on student learning has reached a critical level. A recent longitudinal study of students aged 7 to 16 found that early adoption of social media negatively impacted kids' learning outcomes . Child development researchers and safety advocates have called for an end to screen time in classrooms as literacy rates decline. Generative AI is sending everyone spinning . title: Wonka’s Golden Ticket on Netflix: How it uses AI Gene Wilder
body: Netflix has used artificial intelligence to (in a sense) resurrect a beloved star of stage and screen. As of Wednesday, several episodes of the new Netflix reality competition show Wonka's Golden Ticket are now available on the popular streaming service. This show has been a source of some controversy ever since its announcement over the summer, as its "host" is an AI-generated Gene Wilder who exists in voice form. Reviews of the series from outlets like Variety and NME have criticized the practice, with Variety calling it "ghoulish." You can get a feel for how it works in the trailer, but the essential fact is this: Wilder's AI voice is used to host the game show. Its challenges and general aesthetic are loosely based on the 1971 Willy Wonka The Chocolate Factory film, rather than the original Roald Dahl book or any of the later Hollywood adaptations. Crucially, this AI-generated Wilder is never seen, only heard, with NME calling this version of the deceased actor "blatantly cruel." It's worth mentioning that Wilder's estate gave permission for Netflix to do this, but that hasn't stopped people online from reacting to it in a not-entirely-positive manner. title: You Can See Everything trailer: Nathan Fielder has some questions for Elizabeth Holmes
body: Nathan Fielder first teased his Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything , earlier in Sept. with a tense minute-long exchange between the two. Now, Fielder ( The Rehearsal ) posted A24's official trailer on social media, showing a deeper look into the time he spent with Holmes and her husband, Billy Evans. As Mashable previously reported , You Can See Everything , directed by Fielder and Lance Oppenheim ( Primetime ), chronicles the weeks before Holmes went to prison to serve her over 11-year sentence for fraud. It then spans a three-year journey "into the abyss," according to the film description on A24's website . Fielder lived with Holmes, Evans, and their children on their invitation. The trailer shows Fielder questioning both Holmes and Evans the motives of the former, and whether Evans trusts his wife. Holmes, who founded the bunk health tech company Theranos , insists she has nothing to hide, while her husband insists he's never been suspicious that she's lied to him. The trailer ends with Holmes admitting it's taken her a long time to be OK with anyone seeing her cry. You Can See Everything hits theatres on Oct. 16. title: Daylight saving time: When the clocks change this fall
body: The U.S. is a big country, and we don't all experience the seasons in the same way, but for a lot of us, fall is definitely here. The weather is cooler, football is happening, new iPhones have arrived , and all of that means it's almost time to move the clocks back to close out Daylight Saving Time 2026. Since you're reading this, you're probably wondering exactly when that's supposed to happen. After all, it can get confusing as to whether or not we're even in DST at any given point in time, and the beginning and end of it always sneak up on us every year. Fret not, though, because we have an answer: DST ends this year on Nov. 1 , with clocks moving back from 2 a.m. to 1 a.m. overnight. Yes, that means you get an extra hour of sleep. SEE ALSO: New cat species identified for first time in 100 years This, of course, does not apply to municipalities that don't observe DST, such as Hawaii and most of Arizona. But for the rest of us, we're going to have to manually adjust some of our clocks to reflect the change...after that extra long night of sleep, of course. It's also worth noting that any device you own that's connected to the internet, such as a smartphone or laptop, will most likely change its own time automatically. But if you have an older car or you rely on the clock on your stove, make a note to move it back an hour on Nov. 1.

title: YouTubes microdrama boom is getting bigger
body: Microdramas aren't so micro anymore, at least when it comes to their audience. Microdrama content on YouTube surpassed 6.5 billion views globally in the first half of 2026, according to new data YouTube shared Wednesday at its annual Made on YouTube event in New York City. Watch time for the bite-sized, serialized shows grew more than 50 percent year over year during the same period. And despite a format practically engineered for the vertical smartphone screen, people aren't only watching on their phones. YouTube says views of microdrama content on TVs increased by more than 90 percent year over year during the first half of 2026. YouTube is now giving creators more tools to capitalize on that appetite for short-form, episodic storytelling. The company announced Shorts Series, a new feature that lets creators organize individual Shorts into structured series, complete with custom thumbnails and sequential playback. SEE ALSO: MeganPlays has been on YouTube for 13 years. Here's what she's learned. The idea is to make Shorts behave a little more like episodes of a show. Instead of viewers encountering one video in isolation and having to hunt for the next installment, creators can package them together so audiences can discover a series and keep watching in order. That could be particularly useful for microdramas, which depend on viewers following a story across multiple short episodes. And with audiences increasingly watching those stories on their TVs, the distinction between scrolling through Shorts and sitting down to watch a show is starting to look a little less clear.

title: YouTube lets users customize what content is on their homepage for the first time
body: Unlike some other social media platforms, YouTube is actually pretty good at finding relevant content for users. The platform's recommendation algorithm reviews your watch history, channel subscriptions, and other relevant metrics, then serves up more engaging content to keep viewers entertained and watching. At YouTube's annual Made for YouTube event on Wednesday, the company announced a slew of new features for users that'll make it even easier to find what they want. One feature, called Custom Feeds, will allow users to customize the type of content they see on their YouTube homepage for the first time. Users will be able to create a Custom Feed, telling YouTube, in natural language, exactly what kind of content they want to see in this feed. For example, a user can tell YouTube that it wants a Custom Feed with "long documentaries" or "new DIY creators," and a Custom Feed tab will appear on their YouTube homepage serving up that content. title: YouTube is giving livestream communities more ways to play, pay, and participate
body: Livestream viewers have never been content to just sit back and watch. They chat. They donate. They subscribe. They clip. They make memes . They tell the streamer what to do next. Sometimes, they even feed cats thousands of miles away . Barbara Macdonald remembers that last one particularly well. Macdonald, YouTube 's product manager for Live, has worked on the platform's livestreaming products for more than a decade. Years ago, after YouTube opened an AP I that let creators connect Super Chats and channel memberships to real-world effects, someone hooked a livestream to a cat-feeding station in Russia. A viewer could send money from their own home and watch as food was dispensed for the cats on screen. "I would say Live has always been really focused on how audiences are able to participate and control the action," Macdonald told Mashable. "That's what makes live stand out from asynchronous video." Now, YouTube wants to give creators and their communities a lot more ways to do exactly that. At its annual Made on YouTube event in New York City on Wednesday, the platform is unveiling more than 30 new products and features for creators and viewers, including a slate of updates aimed specifically at livestreaming. Among them are Live Showdowns, timed competitions between creators in which audience participation can influence who wins; an expansion of Watch With, which lets creators build live commentary around other YouTube content; and a pilot that brings YouTube's Auto-Dubbing technology to live video. title: After multiple deaths and injuries, NHTSA is investigating comma.ai
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Aftermarket devices that can boost or augment a vehicle’s native advanced driver assistance systems are the target of a new federal investigation this week. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Office of Defects Investigation says it knows of five crashes in which drivers using devices from comma.ai crashed into stopped or slow-moving cars. Two of the crashes resulted in three deaths, and 11 people were injured in four of the five crashes, some seriously. Comma.ai was the brainchild of George Hotz, who rose to prominence at the start of the last decade by jailbreaking iOS and hacking Sony PlayStations. In 2015, Hotz turned his attention to partially automated driver assists, which were gaining attention following Tesla’s exploits with its Autopilot system. Hotz first modified his own Acura to give it a more advanced driver assist that let him take his hands off the wheel, with the goal of selling his system to Tesla and replacing Mobileye as the company’s supplier. title: America gave up its rare earth edge. China took full advantage.
author: Charles Edward Gehrke, The Conversation
body: Look around you, and you’ll see rare earth elements at work. A phone vibrates because a magnet moves a weight . Its screen was polished with cerium powder. Its connection to the rest of the world crosses oceans on cables amplified with erbium . If you drove today, a rare earth magnet helped you steer, and a cerium compound scrubbed the exhaust . All of these devices function because of 17 metals collectively known as rare earth elements . The scientists who gave the group that name in 1794 created a misnomer. Cerium alone is about as common in the Earth’s crust as copper. However, separating rare earth minerals from one another and from raw ore is intensely difficult. As a result, countries that control the processing of rare earth minerals have a lot of political leverage. Read full article Comments

title: Ray Gunn trailer: Brad Bird blends sci-fi and film noir for a futuristic mystery
body: Netflix has released the trailer for Ray Gunn , the upcoming film from The Incredibles and The Iron Giant director Brad Bird. SEE ALSO: Brad Bird takes us behind the scenes of 'Ray Gunn's massive sci-fi city For Bird, the moment is decades in the making, as he's been working to bring Ray Gunn to the big screen since the '90s. The long-gestating passion project is a blend of sci-fi and film noir that transports viewers to the massive city of Metropia , a world of mile-high skyscrapers, flying cars, and aliens and humans alike. It's a world full of intrigue and corruption, and trying to get to the bottom of all that is the city's lone private eye, the down-on-his-luck Ray Gunn (voiced by Sam Rockwell). (Not to be confused with Australian breakdancer Raygun , who's also found a home on Netflix in the form of a documentary.) Ray and his alien associate Eyera (voiced by Tom Waits) need a job, fast. Otherwise, their business will go under. Luckily for them, a high-profile case lands in their laps, involving volatile media superstar Venus Nova (voiced by Scarlett Johansson) and a grisly murder. But is Venus truly the dangerous femme fatale everyone suspects her to be? Check out the full trailer above to watch sparks fly between Venus and Ray, as well as some serious flying car chases and blaster action. Ray Gunn also stars Alan Tudyk, Matt Berry, Bobby Cannavale, Michael Chernus, Kether Donohue, Michelle Rodriguez, Aasif Mandvi, Matt Jones, Kathryn Hunter, John Ratzenberger, Justin Peck, and Patton Oswalt. Ray Gunn opens in select theaters Dec. 4, and premieres Dec. 18 on Netflix.

title: Brad Bird takes us behind the scenes of Ray Gunns massive sci-fi city
body: The first character you meet in Brad Bird's Ray Gunn isn't the titular private eye (voiced by Sam Rockwell). Nor is it his alien colleague, Eyera (voiced by Tom Waits), nor even pop superstar Venus Nova (voiced by Scarlett Johansson). Instead, it's the film's setting: the massive, retro-futuristic city of Metropia. Ray Gunn 's opening sequence zips viewers through the canyons between Metropia's mile-high buildings. Flying cars and elevated trains transport hordes of humans and aliens alike, but commuters could just as easily rent a jetpack for quick travel. For them, it's business as usual, but for viewers, it's a rollicking introduction to an astounding city. SEE ALSO: How 'Ray Gunn's Venus Nova, pop star of the (retro) future, evolved Bird has been working to make Ray Gunn since the '90s, and he's stressed Metropia's importance from the very beginning. In an introductory note on a script draft from 1996, he wrote that the one character he couldn't adequately capture on the page was Metropia. In this world, he wrote, "Cities are gargantuan jewels that stretch into the heavens." As Ray Gunn moved from page to screen, how did Bird and his team manage to bring the jewel of Metropia to life? At a press day at Netflix's animation studios, Bird and his collaborators broke down the influences and techniques behind the finished version of Metropia, as well as the importance of getting it right. title: Small undersea volcanoes may unleash outsized tsunamis
author: Yook Ji Hun
body: Krakatau, a volcanic island in Indonesia, killed more than 30,000 people when it erupted in 1883. One might assume that volcanic debris posed the major threat, yet many of the victims died from a tsunami caused by the volcanic eruption instead. Volcanoes at sea can pose hazards quite different from those on land, as their impact can vary depending on how the volcanic activity interacts with seawater. In the deep ocean, high water pressure can suppress explosive volcanic activity, making eruptions less destructive. But closer to the surface, the lower water pressure and the high temperatures of volcanic material can cause violent explosions. Yet scientists still do not fully understand the conditions under which volcanic activity can cause a tsunami. To better understand these risks, an international team of researchers examined the 2022 Hunga eruption in Tonga, focusing on the rapid caldera collapse that may have amplified its powerful tsunami. Calderas form when the ground above a magma reservoir collapses as the magma drains away. Comparisons of seafloor topography before and after the eruption showed that a roughly four-kilometer-wide caldera sank by about a kilometer during the eruption. Read full article Comments

title: How to unblock porn sites and stream porn anonymously
body: Online privacy comes at a premium your personal information and internet habits are more valuable and more important than ever before. Everyone wants to know what you get up to, and where you're doing it online, whether it's businesses looking to target you with ads and mailing junk, or scammers who want to exploit you. That's why we recommend you do everything possible to protect yourself online. And if you watch porn , as so many of us do, you should be especially vigilant. We're going to take a wild guess that you'd prefer to be protected from the prying eyes of advertisers, your internet service provider (ISP), and your roommates when you're engaged in the intimate business of visiting porn sites . If sounds right then we recommend investing in a VPN. These cybersecurity services provide everything you need to unblock porn sites and then stream anonymously. What is a VPN? VPNs offer a robust defense for both your data and identity on the internet. VPNs do this by creating a private network that can hide your IP address and connecting you to servers in other countries, which prevents unwanted eyes from spying on your digital and real world location. This ensures that all of your online activity is untraceable and secure. title: My favorite settings to adjust on a Boox e-reader
body: I love e-readers like a Kindle or Kobo because within minutes of turning them on, you can be reading. But I also appreciate the versatility of Boox e-readers , which run on Android and offer readers so much flexibility. With a Boox e-reader, you're no longer trapped in one e-reader's system. Unlike Kobo and Kindle, Boox e-readers are a little less straightforward. Technically, they're E Ink tablets running Android and capable of so much more, but that also means there are more settings and features to dig through. There's a little bit of a learning curve on the Boox, which is initially off-putting. But now that I'm well acquainted with all the settings on a Boox, I really love using this e-reader. So if you just got a Boox tablet or are looking forward to grabbing the new Palma 3 , here are my favorite settings to change on the device. Turn off gestures and add the bar at the bottom You can control your Boox through gestures or a navigation bar, and I much prefer the latter. Credit: Samantha Mangino / Mashable Potentially the best tip I took from the internet is adding the navigation bar to my Boox e-reader. When you set up a Boox, the system prompts you to pick between gesture navigation and a navigation bar. While the gesture system works similarly to what you use on a smartphone or tablet, the navigation bar is far more convenient. It puts common menus like a home button or an option to see all your open apps within reach. You can even customize the navigation bar in system settings. Turn off NaviBall Not using the NaviBall feature on your Boox? Turn it off in settings.

title: Artemis III delays could threaten landing on the moon in 2028
body: NASA 's Artemis III mission is about three months behind schedule, administrator Jared Isaacman says, putting pressure on the agency's plan to launch two moon-landing missions in 2028. In a wide-ranging email to employees on Sunday, Isaacman said Artemis III could launch in the summer of 2027, preserving two opportunities for lunar landings the following year. But that's the "best-case scenario." NASA doesn't plan to put astronauts on the moon during Artemis III. The agency redesigned the mission earlier this year as a crewed flight in Earth orbit, wherein astronauts would rehearse docking the Orion spacecraft with lunar landers built by SpaceX and Blue Origin. The test is intended to practice those crucial space maneuvers close to home and reduce risk before the first Artemis moon landing. The 90-day delay represents a meaningful setback for an agency that has spent this year trying to accelerate the Artemis campaign, leveraging the momentum of the successful Artemis II flight around the moon . It also comes as Isaacman frames the agency's return to the surface as a broader competition with China . That makes NASA's current pace more consequential than a typical schedule slip. "Perpetuating the status quo is not an achievable strategy in this race," Isaacman said. "There is simply too much on the line." SEE ALSO: Scientists want to know what this distant galaxy ate to make it so weird The disclosure of the schedule tension reveals how much ground NASA needs to make up if it wants Artemis IV and V, the first two landing missions of the program, to launch in 2028. title: This GTA V mod lets you destroy Flock cameras. Its creator explains why.
body: Los Santos has a new way to get you in trouble, and you don t even have to commit a crime. A new Grand Theft Auto V mod from artist Morry Kolman, who goes by WTTDOTM online, installs 235 virtual Flock license plate reader cameras around the game s fictional city. Called Grand Theft Automated License Plate Reader , or GTALPR, it brings an extra layer of surveillance to your next drive. And because this is GTA , you can destroy the cameras and collect in-game cash from their wreckage. But the opportunity to blow them up is only part of the point. Kolman wants players to feel what happens when a familiar environment becomes a place where they re constantly being watched. "I m an artist, and much of my practice is based around giving people interesting and engaging ways to learn about the technological and political world around them," Kolman told Mashable. "GTALPR is very much in that vein." For Kolman, a game modeled on an American city, and familiar to millions of players, offered a way to make surveillance tangible. "Suddenly, you're always watched," he added. "With the simple addition of some cameras, the entire environment gains a new passive layer of hostility." Bringing Flock s camera network to Los Santos In the real world, Flock s automated license plate readers capture vehicle images and enable police to search for vehicles and receive alerts about those on watchlists. Flock pitches the technology as a way to help law enforcement locate wanted vehicles. title: Woman's brain worm infection confirmed after eggs grow tails in lab test
author: Beth Mole
body: Out of nowhere, a woman's right arm and leg started shaking uncontrollably. In the moments leading up to the experience, she seemed well; she had no headache, confusion, or weakness. But for about a minute, half of her body juddered. The woman, a rice farmer in the Philippines, headed to the emergency department. There, doctors gave her a physical exam and found nothing out of the ordinary. Then they took a look at her brain. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a bright cluster of nodules surrounded by fluid in her left frontal lobe. The doctors had an immediate guess as to what they were: worm eggs. An MRI of the woman's brain showing nodules. Credit: NEJM, 2026 In a case report published in the latest issue of the New England Journal of Medicine , doctors write that they suspected the woman had neuroschistosomiasis, an uncommon complication of an infection with a Schistosoma parasitic worm, aka a blood fluke. In the Philippines, the most common fluke is S. japonicum . It's also found in China and part of Indonesia; despite its name, it has been eliminated from Japan. Read full article Comments

title: Big banks are worried AI agents could increase the risk of scams and fraud
body: While AI true believers worry about doom-and-gloom scenarios of AI destroying the world , some major financial institutions are sounding the alarm over a more grounded AI-related concern: scams. On Tuesday, a consortium of big global banks put out a " principles paper " detailing their apprehensions regarding AI assistants as it relates to commerce. It also details principles that they would like to see followed as AI companies develop and continue to work on the technology. Namely, the banks are concerned that AI agents empowered to act on behalf of customers will lose money to scams and fraud and, in turn, hurt merchants. "As highly regulated financial entities, we are focused on managing risk effectively as emerging technologies arise," reads the opening of the paper. "Consumers are unclear if AI agents will act in their interests." "They are concerned that AI agents may buy the wrong thing or spend too much or even worse, lose their money to scams and fraud," the paper continues. "They are not sure whether they will be protected or who they ​will need to go ​to if things ⁠go wrong." The paper, called Building Trust in Agentic Commerce , was published by Bank of America, Capital One, ASB Bank, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, ING Group, and NatWest Group. Agentic commerce introduces new safety risks, with potential for higher rates of scams, fraud and disputes. title: Waymo now offering transit rewards to riders
body: Waymo just announced a new transit rewards program that incentivizes pairing robotaxi rides with public transit. The transit rewards program is now available to Waymo employees in the San Francisco Bay Area, but it will open to the Bay Area public in a few weeks, according to the Google-owned autonomous rideshare company. The program requires a Visa credit or debit tap-to-pay card (rival credit card Mastercard already offers transit incentives on most major U.S. systems, many of which already offer tap-to-pay in lieu of transit cards or tokens). "To participate, riders will link their Visa card in the Waymo app," according to a statement from Waymo. "When riders in the SF Bay Area use their Visa card to take a Waymo trip and public transit within 2 hours of each other, we will automatically issue $2.85 in Waymo Cash, which is the cost of a bus fare in San Francisco." The Waymo Cash is loaded into the app and can be used for future robotaxi rides. Over two dozen San Francisco Bay Area transit agencies are participating in Waymo's rewards program, according to the company. In announcing the rewards, Waymo also stated the company is leasing 40 parking spots at stations within the Caltrain commuter system , which covers a wide swath of the Bay Area. Waymo vehicles will occupy the parking spots and be available to take riders from train stations to their destinations. title: Microsoft disrupts AI-assisted platform that compromised 12,000 accounts
author: Dan Goodin
body: Microsoft said Tuesday that it led an industry-wide disruption of a subscription-based scam platform that used an AI chatbot to compromise 12,000 Microsoft accounts over a few-month span. Named EvilTokens, the platform was introduced over a Telegram channel in February and charged an initial $1,500 fee and a recurring $500 charge each month after that. EvilTokens provided a single service for streamlining most steps required to compromise email accounts in large numbers. From there, the platform helped customers analyze inboxes, select targets that would provide the biggest potential payouts, and draft follow-up emails that provided realistic ruses for tricking company employees into transferring funds to attacker-controlled accounts. Minutes, not days “While EvilTokens helped cybercriminals access email accounts, at the center of the service was an AI-style chatbot that could analyze a victim’s inbox and help criminals identify trusted relationships, payment authorizations, and sensitive responsibilities, as well as other circumstances where fraud was most likely to succeed,” Microsoft said . “The platform could even recommend fraud strategies, including drafting messages that impersonated trusted contacts to help criminals trick victims into taking action.” Read full article Comments

body: X has introduced a new way for users to be contacted on its messaging service without sharing a phone number or following each other. The company launched X Numbers on Tuesday , giving XChat users a private code they can share with people who need to message or call them without a mutual follow. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. According to X's Help Center , anyone who enters a user's enabled X Number can message them even if the user doesn't follow them or has a closed inbox. Those conversations go straight to the inbox instead of message requests, and the sender can also place calls, depending on the recipient's call settings. Despite its name, X says an X Number isn't a phone number. It's also separate from the safety numbers Chat uses to verify identities in encrypted conversations. SEE ALSO: Elon Musk's SpacexAI faces another lawsuit from child sexual abuse survivor The feature is optional, and X says users can turn it off or refresh it at any time. Refreshing generates a new code, cutting off new contacts who only have the old one. X notes that people a user has already messaged can see their X Number and may share it with others, though a "Hide from others" setting can prevent that. The company also says users will be notified when someone contacts them through the code. To set one up, X says users can open Chat, enter their Chat PIN if prompted, open the inbox dropdown menu, and tap "Number." title: Adobe Premiere finally brings powerful video editing to Android, and it's free
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Video editing has never been Android's strong suit. While Apple has long offered iMovie for iPhone and iPad, Google has never had a comparable offering. Adobe is now stepping up to fill this feature gap with a proper version of Premiere. The app is now available in the Play Store for almost all Android devices, and it's free (mostly). Android's version of Premiere doesn't offer all the features you'd get in the desktop application, but it's a big step up from the soon-to-be-retired Premiere Rush app. You can import as many video tracks as you want, trim them, split them, add effects, and export videos in up to 4K resolution. It can even extract audio from clips, reduce background noise, and add voiceovers. The app emphasizes the YouTube Short format, even defaulting your video outputs to portrait 16:9, but you can change that to something more traditional. On a standard smartphone, the app splits the screen with the timeline at the bottom and preview up top. Adobe says that Premiere is optimized for multiple form factors. If you have a foldable phone, the UI adjusts to give you more breathing room, placing the timeline to the right of the video. That makes sense as the default, as Premiere wants you to make YouTube Shorts, but if you're working with something wider, there's a layout toggle that puts the widescreen video above the expanded timeline. The split is also adjustable if you want to make your video or timeline larger. Read full article Comments

body: It'd be presumptuous to say, but the Silent Hill franchise might be back. That is to say, if you consider Silent Hill 2 Remake to be a fluke, and Silent Hill f's critical success to be an aberration, then you'd hate to hear that Silent Hill: Townfall the newest game from Konami and developers Screen Burn Interactive is also a very good game. If you're a diehard about the canon of Silent Hill, you're not going to like this. Townfall is the latest installment in the psychological survival horror franchise, and it's the first full game to shift to first-person instead of over-the-shoulder. That brings us to Townfall , set in 1990's Scotland and featuring, to date, Silent Hill's first Black protagonist. title: Review: Resident Evil is the fresh take this flagging franchise really needed
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: I was on the fence about going to see the latest Resident Evil reboot to review, given how uninspired the prior reboot attempt in 2021 turned out to be. But director Zach Cregger gave us last year's phenomenal Weapons, and early word of mouth was extremely positive, so I took a chance. I'm glad I did, because the film is terrific. Cregger's distinctive sensibility is just what the flagging franchise needed: a truly fresh take on a well-trodden fictional world that blends horror, humor, and some pretty over-the-top gore in just the right ratios. And you don't need to be a Resident Evil franchise fan to enjoy it. (Spoilers below, but we'll give you a heads-up before any major reveals.) When the first Resident Evil game debuted in 1996, it was an immediate commercial and critical success, spawning several sequel games, comics, novels, and a very lucrative film franchise directed by Paul W.S. Anderson and starring Milla Jovovich. Reviews were mixed, despite the films’ massive box office success. The first reboot, Welcome to Raccoon City (2021) , was critically panned and had a disappointing box office, grossing just $42 million globally against its $25 million budget. The studio nixed its plans for a direct sequel, and a 2022 Netflix series was also canceled after a less-than-stellar first season. Read full article Comments

As TechSpot notes, a recent industry study found the memory market now resembles, on a per-unit basis, conditions from nearly two decades ago. title: Effort begins to fill the void left by terminated US climate report
author: Scott K. Johnson
body: Last year, the Trump administration did what it could to shut down work on the next US National Climate Assessment, eliminating funding for the US Global Change Research Program and booting hundreds of contributing authors. The administration even took past reports offline, forcing others to host copies so the information would still be accessible. And this all comes despite the fact that these reports are legally required. Later in the year, the American Geophysical Union and American Meteorological Society announced an effort to give researchers a central place to compile the kind of work that would have fed the next US report, as well as potential regional and local reports. This “ US Climate Collection ” works differently from the US Global Change Research Program or the International Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). Rather than facilitating the writing of a giant, coordinated report, the groups are inviting teams of researchers to publish peer-reviewed papers in scientific journals, which will then be added to a centralized resource for future report-writers. The first paper has now been added to that collection. It’s the work of 149 authors (many of whom had been working on the US report), and it is actually being published in two journals—one operated by the American Geophysical Union and one by the American Meteorological Society. That’s because this paper is intended to provide a roadmap to prioritize future contributions. Read full article Comments

title: Meta’s Muse reportedly has zero-day vulnerability that lets attackers take over your Mac
body: Meta launched its new AI assistant Muse to much fanfare earlier this month. Now, just a few weeks later, a zero-day vulnerability has reportedly been discovered that could put access to your entire Mac computer in the wrong hands. (Meta currently does not have a Windows version of Muse for PC.) macOS security expert Patrick Wardle posted on X about the vulnerability with the Muse app. According to Wardle, and as first covered by Ars Technica , the vulnerability lets "local malware/attackers invisibly hijack" a user's Mac. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Wadle explains that thanks to the macOS permissions that Muse requires, an attacker could access and change the endpoint where transcription for dictation occurs. The server address is pointed to one that belongs to Meta, but with this change, the attacker could then gain access to the token that controls the Muse account. From there, the attacker doesn't need to deploy any specific trojan or code to steal data from a user's machine, Wardle explained. They can simply take control of Muse to do so. As a personal AI agent, Muse is able to help complete tasks and perform actions on a user's computer. This requires that a user give Muse a lot of permissions on their device, more than a user would provide to most other third-party applications. Other popular AI agents like OpenClaw have the same security risks . Meta predicted the potential security issues with Muse requiring so many system permissions. body: This has been an astoundingly brutal year for Xbox , and the carnage continued on Tuesday. Microsoft's gaming division announced in a blog post that it's laying off 268 people across its first-party studios, on top of 1,600 roles that were cut in July . According to Xbox executive Matt Booty, Tuesday's cuts bring us to roughly 75 percent of all currently planned cuts to Xbox's payroll, which means more layoffs are presumably coming. For the employees who do remain, Xbox is also reshuffling its development deck to a severe degree. Perhaps most notably, the celebrated Halo franchise is now under the control of Xbox subsidiary Activision, maker of Call of Duty . Halo Studios, which was created with the sole purpose of making Halo games, will live on as a support studio for the time being. Age of Empires developer World's Edge and Sea of Thieves developer Rare are also under the Activision umbrella now. Beyond that, Elder Scrolls and Fallout developer Bethesda has taken Pentiment and Avowed developer Obsidian under its wing. Mobile game developer King is fusing with Microsoft Casual Games, too. Lastly, Playground Games and Turn 10 will join forces to be the stewards of both the Fable and Forza franchises. Many of those partnerships already existed in a sense, as Obsidian had worked with Bethesda before, while the same is true of Playground and Turn 10, but they're seemingly more formalized now. Today, the company announced a radical restructuring of its internal studios that is seemingly designed to reduce that "independence" for the teams behind some of gaming's biggest franchises. The biggest apparent change is for the Halo franchise, which will now be under the remit of Call of Duty maker Activision. Halo Studios (formerly 343 Industries), which recently released Halo: Campaign Evolved , will remain as just a "small team" to support the player community, Microsoft said, with the remaining staffing roles eliminated as part of 268 newly announced layoffs. title: Protests for Germany’s car industry as job losses loom
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: The future is looking increasingly bleak for Germany’s automotive industry. Since the turn of the century, car makers have been among the crown jewels of the German economy, punching above their weight in terms of investment and innovation. But those companies are now facing multiple problems at once, from declining demand at home and stronger competition from abroad to the cost of punitive and arbitrary new tariffs, on top of preexisting structural challenges like an aging workforce and a slow recovery from COVID. Total automotive sales in Europe have fallen from a peak of almost 18 million in 2019 to around 13 million in 2025, and some share of that smaller market is increasingly going to new entrants from China, which has its own spare automotive production capacity problem to worry about. And while the US market has always been the most profitable for German car exports, that was before the imposition of new import tariffs, which currently stand at 25 percent but could be subject to change at any time. Factory closures now seem not just possible but likely, something that would have been unthinkable just a few years ago. Earlier this summer, news emerged that Volkswagen Group is considering closing four of its German factories to prepare for the future. Things have not gotten much better for VW Group in the months since that news broke. Read full article Comments

This means, if it's a clear night, you'll have ample opportunity to spot some features on its surface. What can you see? Keep reading to find out. What is today s Moon phase? As of Tuesday, Sept. 22, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 81% of its surface visible. Without the assistance of visual aids, you should be able to spot the Mare Vaporum, Mare Fecunditatis, and the Tycho Crater. If you have binoculars, they'll also help you see the Mare Nectaris, Alphonsus Crater, and the Mare Frigoris. Plus, if you have access to a telescope, you'll see the Apollo 12 and 15 landing spots, as well as the Rima Hyginus. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on September 26. What are Moon phases? The Moon doesn't look the same from night to night. As it travels around Earth, which takes about 29.5 days, we see different portions of its illuminated side. This is what creates the lunar phases, with the Moon gradually progressing from a thin crescent to a half Moon and then a Full Moon before the cycle starts over. According to NASA , the phase we see is determined by the Moon's position relative to both Earth and the Sun. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). body: Last week, The New York Times reported that an internal memo had been quietly distributed across US Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) field offices, directing staff to radically reinterpret the Endangered Species Act (ESA) in a move that blindsided conservationists. Staffers were essentially asked to start looking the other way when private interests cause preventable deaths of vulnerable animals. Instead of prohibiting habitat modifications that injure animals or cause accidental deaths, the ESA will now only prohibit actions “specifically intending to target an animal,” FWS Director Brian Nesvik instructed staff in the September 14 memo. “A vessel that inadvertently strikes a whale has not taken it because the vessel’s course was not set against the whale,” Nesvik’s memo said. “Felling a tree is not a take of the bats roosting in it unless the tree is felled for the purpose of killing or capturing them.” Read full article Comments

title: Dyson’s most overengineered gadget may have a waterproofing problem
author: Jeremy White, wired.com
body: There's always a danger in over-complicating products. Simple is so often best. The apocryphal story of NASA spending millions crafting a space pen while Soviet cosmonauts used a pencil is often cited as a prime example, even if it's actually not true . Perhaps it's not surprising that Dyson has got into hot water trying to reinvent the electric toothbrush . The Chinese invented the first bristle toothbrush during the Ming dynasty. That concept muddled along quite nicely until 1937, when Tomlinson Moseley filed a patent for the earliest electric toothbrush. After more than 400 years, the Motodent marked the beginning of an evolutionary shift from manual brushing to powered oral care. Having had considerable success reimagining established product categories such as stick vacuums and premium hair dryers —though not so much air-purifying headphones —the company earlier this month, with great fanfare, unveiled the next leap forward for teeth: the $499 Dyson CameraJet with a tiny camera to aim streams of rinsing fluid into the gaps between your teeth. title: Sex recession is real but complicated, Kinsey reports
body: The sex lives of young adults or lack thereof have been subject to scrutiny over the past few years. Much hand-wringing has occurred over whether Gen Z is sexually repressed , or whether there's a "sex recession" happening. Now, we have some new data about it. In a study by the Kinsey Institute, Playboy, and emergency contraceptive brand Julie, "The State of Sex Among Gen Z," the sex recession question is answered, but it's not clean-cut. The report includes findings from 2,373 U.S. adults between 18 and 29. That breaks down into 48 percent men and 48 percent women, 63 percent heterosexual, 53 percent single, and 42 percent in relationships. SEE ALSO: A 'masturbation consultant' for an AI companion company tells all A major finding of the study is that the sex recession appears to be real, but it's complicated. There's no one explanation for why this is happening; economic, technological, psychological, and social factors all play a part. And while most young adults report low levels of sexual activity, they have moderate to high sexual desire. Less sex, partnered or solo Previous reports found that today's young adults are having less sex than those of years past. The State of Sex Among Gen Z found that 29 percent of participants had no sexual partners in the last three months, and 19 percent have never had a partner. Thirty-one percent aren't sexually active. Around a third (36 percent) haven't even masturbated in the last three months. Of those who have had sex in the last quarter, 45 percent had one partner. title: Control Resonant is a fascinating experiment, but not an entirely successful one
body: When you play as many video games as I do, only a select few really stick in your mind for years after you finish them. Control , a 2019 action-adventure game, was one of those. Mashable gave Control its Game of the Year award that year, and for good reason: It's a mind-bending and totally sick shooter that can be cleanly summarized as "you play as a Jedi with a gun in a haunted office building." It was, at the time, the best synthesis of developer Remedy's signature style with actually competent gunplay, something the studio had struggled with at points in the past. I'd argue it was only surpassed by 2023's Alan Wake II in that regard, but that's like choosing a favorite child. I wish I was as enthusiastic about Control Resonant , the new follow-up to the 2019 original that I am still working my way through. But, while Resonant maintains the creepy vibes, non-Euclidean geometry, and action combat that make you feel extremely cool on a regular basis of the original, its new setting of a supernaturally warped Manhattan significantly reduces the charm in both an aesthetic and mechanical sense. title: NASA chief: I'm only interested in "good deals" from international partners
author: Stephen Clark
body: NASA must be more selective in the way it forges international partnerships as the race to the Moon transforms from a battle for national prestige between the United States and China into a high-stakes competition for extraterrestrial real estate and resources, the agency's administrator said. Jared Isaacman, now in his 10th month at the helm of the world's largest civilian space agency, told a gathering of military leaders and defense contractors last week near Washington, DC, that the 21st century race to the Moon is more than a battle of ideologies. The sweet spot for a Moon base, Isaacman said, is a relatively small region near the lunar south pole, and there are tangible implications for who gets there first. The Moon's south pole harbors substantial quantities of water ice concentrated on the floors of craters away from the reach of sublimating rays of sunlight. The ice inside these eternally dark craters could be used to supply water, air, and rocket fuel for a Moon base, supporting a permanent settlement and providing a springboard for future expeditions to Mars. "For a generation told to keep things casual and see where they go, saying you want marriage can almost feel countercultural," said Lauren DeFord, director of brand marketing at Match Group, in a press release shared with Mashable. "Built for people dating with marriage in mind, Upward is a home for singles who know what they want, hold strong standards and believe dating should lead somewhere." SEE ALSO: FBI warned ICE agents of fake 'tradwife' dating profiles The shift comes amid a deluge of " tradwife " content on social media, of young women rejecting (or claiming to reject) modern attitudes for more traditional gender roles in their relationships. The trend has reached a new peak in 2026 with Yesteryear , a novel about a tradwife influencer who wakes up in 1855, which has been on the New York Times bestsellers list for 23 weeks. For several years, young adults have also been decrying hookup culture and casual sex , while also reportedly having less sex than in generations past. body: What are the most comfortable headphones? Credit: Alex Bracetti / Mashable The most comfortable earbuds and headphones shouldn't cause ear fatigue or pain, even after hours of listening to music or podcasts. After extensive testing, we selected the five most comfortable headphones based on price, performance, and purpose. However, one product in particular stood out, and it's the one with "Comfort" literally in the name. Our audio reviewers are unanimous on this point: Bose QuietComfort Ultra (Gen 2) are the most comfortable headphones available right now. Read on to find out what other pairs emerged as the top choices, including picks for those who want top-tier noise cancellation . In-ear, on-ear, or over-ear? If you're looking for comfort above all, over-ear headphones are almost always the way to go. They just wear better than earbuds or on-ear models. The latter is harsher on your ears, which can cause serious discomfort, depending on how long you wear them. In-ear buds are generally more comfortable than on-ear headphones, but they can still begin to hurt after just a few hours (they are jammed inside your ears, after all). Although over-ear headphones are bulkier and less portable, it's worth the trade-off for comfort's sake. Plus, over-ear headphones can be safer for your ears compared to earbuds because the sound isn't being funneled directly into your ear canal. They also provide extra noise cancellation . title: RatHat is a new Android malware that records your screen touches to steal passwords
body: Beware: There's a new malware making the rounds and it's targeting your Android device. Cybersecurity researchers at Zimperium recently discovered a new strain of Android malware, called RatHat, and have linked it to threat actors based out of China. "RatHat incorporates novel techniques for persistence and leverages generative AI for operational control," Zimperium's zLabs researchers said in a report . As the cybersecurity firm Malwarebytes explains, "RatHat gives a live AI assistant the keys to the accessibility tree of the infected device." This unique weaponization of AI allows the attacker to figure out "where to tap or scroll, rather than following a hardcoded script." As with most malware, RatHat initially infects the device through social engineering tactics. The attacker convinces a target to download a seemingly legit app, such as Google Chrome, through a fake website posing as the Google Play Store. The user downloads the app but unknowingly installs the RatHat malware on their device. SEE ALSO: Malware found hidden inside popular 'Meccha Chameleon' game maps From there, RatHat requests accessibility permissions while still masked as a legitimate application. Once the target provides RatHat with those permissions, the malware activates Wireless Debugging under Developer Options. RatHate weaponizes this actual Android developer feature to pair with the device. With this access, RatHat is able to capture text messages and create overlays on targeted apps, steal passwords, and multi-factor authentication codes in the process. title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day
author: Dan Goodin
body: Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg has gone to great lengths to hype the security of its new AI assistant Muse, claiming it is “built from the ground up for privacy and security.” A zero-day vulnerability that gives locally run apps and terminal commands complete control of the agent raises serious doubts. Further raising questions, Amazon on Sunday began blocking Muse from its site. Meta introduced Muse a few weeks ago. The assistant “books appointments, fills out forms and handles customer service,” “proactively takes tasks off your plate,” and can “make purchases, generate images, create documents, and connect with your favorite apps and services.” The macOS app (curiously, there’s no Windows version) also works with a user’s WhatsApp, email, calendar, and social media accounts. When a task requires a tool that doesn’t exist, Muse creates one on the fly. Meta doth hype Muse security too much Of course, for Muse to do any of these things, users must first give it access to their accounts. This includes authenticating the assistant to each service and, because the app runs on macOS, giving it permissions to a broad range of operating system-restricted device resources like writing files to disk, accessing the mic and camera, and monitoring location and calendars. Apple has spent years developing these defenses to prevent installed apps or commands entered into the terminal from accessing these resources, clearly because the company considers them a security threat. Muse completely undoes these default measures. Read full article Comments

title: Snapchat will turn your messages into songs — if you pay for Lens+
body: Ever wanted to hear your group chat's worst message set to a pop chorus? Snapchat can do that now. Snap announced a batch of new AI features for Lens+ , its premium tier, on Monday, and the headliner is Create Song. Press and hold a message in a chat, tap Create Song, and pick a genre such as pop or rock. Snapchat turns your message into a short original track, and you can preview it before sending it to your friend. Credit: Snapchat If your chats are more visual than musical, the rest of the update is for you. AI Photoshoot is built to rescue near-miss Snaps, fixing shots where someone blinked, looked away, made a funny face, or got caught in bad lighting. Credit: Snapchat And AI Remix lets subscribers take a Snap a friend sent and reimagine it in a new style as a reply. There's also a sticker tool that restyles custom, saved, or received Stickers, and AI-enhanced fonts that can turn captions into bubble letters, spray paint, foam, or fuzzy textures. Credit: Snapchat Credit: Snapchat For anyone who has lost track of Snap's subscription tiers, Lens+ launched last year as a tier within Snapchat+, which Snap says now has more than 25 million subscribers worldwide. It already gave subscribers exclusive Lenses and AR effects, along with generative tools like the Imagine Lens for image generation and AI Clips, which turns a single photo into a five-second video. Those tools run on a monthly generation allowance, and Lens+ costs $7.99 a month. As for when you can try it, the new features are rolling out now in all markets where Lens+ is available, though Snap says access may vary

title: Military milestone: Ukrainian naval drone sinks Russian kamikaze drone boat
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: In the world’s first clash of the drone boats, a Ukrainian naval drone destroyed a Russian explosive drone boat using a remote-controlled machine gun turret. This comes as the war in Ukraine has already seen widespread deployment of such uncrewed surface vessels in combat, along with swarms of flying attack drones and ground robots. The lopsided battle took place on September 12 when members of Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence detected the Russian uncrewed surface vessel (USV) in the Black Sea and directed a Ukrainian Navy drone boat to intercept. The Russian vessel was “positively identified” as an Orcan surface drone with a “jet ski type steerable water jet” designed to ram targets and explode, according to naval analyst HI Sutton in Naval News . Such Orcan drones have already been used to attack Ukrainian ports and ships. These often work in coordination with flying drones such as Russian Geran drones that provide aerial reconnaissance and can boost communication between drone operators and drone boats, Sutton explained. title: Saudi Arabia wants a car industry, launches Ceer with two EVs
author: Chad Kirchner
body: Ceer provided flights from Detroit to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and accommodation so Ars could visit the factory. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. KING ABDULLAH ECONOMIC CITY, Saudi Arabia—It may come as a surprise to some, but Saudi Arabia has never had a domestic automaker. That changes with Ceer. A joint venture between the country’s Public Investment Fund and Foxconn, it’s the Kingdom’s first home-grown automaker and a significant part of Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 plan to diversify its economy away from oil production and bring technological innovation locally by the end of the decade. Ceer in Arabic means to “drive forward,” and this forward-looking approach applies to the vehicle lineup. The flagship vehicles you see here—the Exobot sedan and SUV—are demonstrations of what the company is capable of and the vision it sees for future vehicles in the portfolio. It plans to have seven new cars in its portfolio by 2030—some of which will be hybrids—and while that doesn’t currently include sales outside the GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) region, Ceer says it's building a competitive, world-class product and that if the demand is there, expansion is possible. title: Paramount settles lawsuit blocking $110 billion Warner Bros. merger
body: Paramount has reached a settlement with California and the 11 other states that sued to block its planned $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The settlement removes a major roadblock standing in the way of the massive media merger. According to the proposed consent decree filed with the court, it includes requirements like minimum numbers of theatrical film releases over the next five years, starting with 30 in year one and two, and 32 in the following years, and a commitment to spend at least $300 million more on production in the US compared to what the companies spent in 2025. That design choice was on purpose: Not everyone likes to have earbuds with foamy seals stuck in their ear canal (that's what the best noise-cancelling earbuds do to get additional passive noise cancellation). title: Google confirms Gemini models hacked three companies in May 2026
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: It has become increasingly common for AI firms to announce that their latest and most capable models engaged in unauthorized real-world hacking. Google, which has been slow to release frontier Gemini models in recent months, has been absent from the "rogue AI" conversation until now. Following a Wall Street Journal report, Google has confirmed that Gemini models hacked three companies during a May 2026 test, but the nature of the intrusion isn't as troubling (or impressive) as previous AI hacks. The hack took place during a test conducted by cybersecurity firm Irregular. A collection of Gemini models were taking part in a "capture the flag" exercise intended to test the AI's cybersecurity capabilities in a closed environment. The AI was instructed to retrieve information from a fake company (which shared a name with a real company) within this environment. Irregular was not supposed to allow the model to operate outside its servers, but due to a misconfiguration, Gemini was able to access the Internet. When Gemini started snooping around the web, it targeted real infrastructure instead of the fakes. For one of the three hacks, Gemini simply guessed passwords until it accessed a company's online services. In the other two instances, Gemini searched public software repositories until it found login credentials for companies that had been accidentally included. Read full article Comments

title: Russel Vought will reportedly be given veto power over all NIH grants
author: John Timmer
body: On Friday, The Washington Post reported on a contentious White House meeting in which the director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Jay Bhattacharya, tried to fend off yet another effort to place funding decisions under political control. The move came from Russell Vought, head of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), which has sought to limit and control research funds. The Post suggested that Bhattacharya ended up on the losing side of the fight. This initial leak has been confirmed and expanded on by outlets such as The New York Times and Politico . It now appears that the administration is drafting an executive order that would give Vought veto power over every individual grant awarded by the NIH. If at first you don't succeed The NIH is the largest funder of biomedical research on the planet, and its $47 billion budget is larger than that of the next 10 research funders combined. Its funding, distributed largely through grants to academic researchers at universities, supports everything from basic biological research to clinical trials and has helped the biotechnology industry flourish. title: Googlebooks launch October 4 starting at $899—here are the five models you can preorder today
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Google is ready to take a swing at laptops... again. The company has had a lot of success in phones, but it has struggled to parlay that into an effective strategy for larger screens. Chromebooks have been fine as a budget option, but it seems like Google has accepted they'll never compete with macOS or Windows. That's where Googlebooks come in. These new Android-powered laptops are intended to be "real" computers, featuring premium hardware, on-device apps, and powerful development tools. After the Googlebook reveal at I/O this year , Google's partners are now ready to sell you one. The first Googlebooks are available from several OEMs that have been making Chromebooks over the years, but don't expect Chromebook pricing. There's only one model under a grand, and the rest are well above that. Familiar hardware The bulk of Chromebooks have been budget machines, and they looked the part. Googlebooks, however, feature bright OLED screens, metal builds, big haptic trackpads, and the Glowbar. All the machines have this illuminated bar on the lid, but it doesn't do much for now. It lights up when the device boots and can display battery level, but Google says it's going to release an API for developers to add more features. Read full article Comments

Your computer didn't need much storage, Pichai explained, or any fancy hardware, because the cloud would do the work. title: The first 5 Googlebook laptops are here, with an OS that blends Android and Gemini
body: For decades, laptop shoppers have really only had two choices: Mac or PC? Now, there's a third option: the Googlebook. Starting today, the first five Googlebook devices are now available for preorder (they officially launch on Oct. 4), with Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo each launching a new device. Earlier this year, Google announced the imminent arrival of Googlebooks , a new generation of premium AI laptops running on an entirely new operating system, which blends elements of Android, ChromeOS, and Gemini. (A Google spokesperson confirmed the new operating system is called Googlebook OS.) Unlike Chromebooks, which are generally cheaper, stripped-down laptops, the new Googlebook devices feature a baseline 16GB of RAM, are made with premium materials such as aluminum and magnesium, and feature much more impressive chipsets. They're also priced more like MacBooks than Chromebooks . All the devices are ultra-thin and lightweight, and except for the Dell, they all come with OLED displays. title: John Oliver mocks soon-to-be business daddy David Ellison
body: John Oliver 's main target was American health care conglomerate UnitedHealth Group and its insurance arm, UnitedHealthcare, during Last Week Tonight on Sunday. But the host also found time to get in a quick dig at David Ellison, the CEO of Paramount Skydance, who is currently in the process of trying to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery. If the deal closes, Ellison's company would also own WBD subsidiary HBO, which airs Oliver's show. "Having access to wealthy parents just cannot be the system to get badly-needed healthcare, even if it is apparently the system that lets you be in charge of HBO," says Oliver, bringing up a photo of Ellison alongside his billionaire father, Larry Ellison, who personally pledged $40 billion to support Paramount's bid. "Yeah, my soon-to-be business daddy has a literal business daddy, and to be very clear, I deeply respect that. And I would never make fun of you for it, unlike that pesky Stephen Colbert.
